walkthroughs.body_html: Imagine both demand AND supply rise. Quantity definitely increases, but price is indeterminate — depends on which shift is bigger. Top-band answers always state when an outcome is uncertain and explain WHY.

Use point-explanation-application-link chains. Example: 'Cheap solar panels (point) lower production costs (explain), so EV supply shifts right (apply), raising equilibrium quantity and lowering price (link).' Repeat 2–3 times, then evaluate.

Strong answers consider time-lag (markets don't adjust instantly), magnitude (small vs large shifts), and context (luxury vs necessity good). Use words like 'however', 'in the short run', 'depends on'.

mcqs.q: Both demand AND supply for trainers increase. Which outcome is CERTAIN?
options: Price rises
Quantity rises
Price falls
Quantity falls

mcqs.q: Bus journeys are typically an inferior good. If incomes rise, what happens?
options: Demand shifts right
Demand shifts left
Supply shifts right
No change

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
A sustained rise in the general price level over time — reducing the purchasing power of money. Measured by the percentage change in a price index.
Inflation is when prices are high.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
Inflation is when the economy grows too fast.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
